item.text: {"verdict":"revise","issues":[{"severity":"error","source_ids":["brief-a:6","brief-a:7","brief-a:46","brief-a:closing.p1"],"location":"opening.transitions; opening schedule_callback tool","message":"The callback-success route has no successful route into close_stage. The only route out of opening to close_stage is a semantic match described as a non-callback terminal disposition; the fallback returns to opening. After a valid callback offer is scheduled successfully, that route can send the next turn back to opening, allowing another callback/tool call or leaving the call open instead of closing not_reached/callback. A callback API failure also has no source-legal recovery/closure path specified by the workflow.","fix":"Track a validated callback disposition and the current schedule_callback receipt. Route to close_stage only after the required action succeeds; on failure, keep the dialogue actionable and handle the failure without claiming callback was scheduled or inventing another disposition."},{"severity":"error","source_ids":["brief-a:32","brief-a:41","brief-a:42","brief-a:46","brief-a:closing.p1"],"location":"opening.transitions; identity.transitions; negotiation.transitions; transfer_to_agent tools","message":"Transfer actions are exposed as dialogue tools, but no transition reliably routes to close_stage after a successful transfer. In negotiation, the only terminal route is model-triggered matches_intent; if the model instead extracts a terminal-looking candidate and the always route is selected, it remains in negotiation. The prompt's instruction to close after transfer does not establish actual receipt-gated routing. The same issue exists for opening's human-insistence transfer and identity's refusal/human paths.","fix":"Add receipt-gated terminal routing for each transfer branch, with queue and current-call success validated before close; ensure deterministic routes cannot starve required terminal routes."},{"severity":"error","source_ids":["brief-a:14","brief-a:15","brief-a:46","brief-a:closing.p1"],"location":"identity.transitions","message":"The three-wrong-answer and second-refusal closures depend only on matches_intent text, with no deterministic check of wrong_answers_left or a trusted refusal count. Candidate extraction can misclassify an answer or refusal, and API failure/unreadable DOB results are not differentiated by a trusted state route. This creates a plausible path to close incorrectly or loop past the specified stop condition.","fix":"Maintain trusted counts from verify_identity application results and source-validated refusal events; route to the required not_verified disposition only when those facts establish it."},{"severity":"error","source_ids":["brief-a:37","brief-a:46","brief-a:closing.p1"],"location":"negotiation.tools.create_promise; negotiation.transitions; close_stage","message":"create_promise retry and service_error disposition are described in prose, but the actual transitions are only a semantic terminal match and unconditional self-route. A failed first call does not deterministically force exactly one retry, and a second failed call does not establish the required no_promise/service_error closure. The conversation can remain in negotiation, repeat/refuse terms, or claim a different disposition.","fix":"Track the current product's promise attempt and actual data.ok receipt. After the first failure keep the action available for one retry; after the second failure route to close_stage with no_promise/service_error."},{"severity":"warning","source_ids":["brief-a:46","brief-a:47"],"location":"close_stage.transitions; close_call tool","message":"The workflow says close_call is exactly once and last, but the unsuccessful close_call path loops back to close_stage and exposes close_call again. Since the API says a failed 200/500 records nothing and may be repeated, this is not necessarily forbidden, but the prose says exactly one close_call and provides no reconciliation for failure.","fix":"Clarify whether a failed close_call may be retried; if permitted, state the retry limit and ensure no duplicate successful close is possible."}],"counterexamples":[{"source_ids":["brief-a:6","brief-a:46"],"scenario":"A relative offers a valid callback for today at 18:00, later than now. schedule_callback returns data.ok=true. On the next turn the deterministic always route in opening returns to opening; there is no callback-specific receipt route to close_stage.","expected_output":"After the successful schedule_callback receipt, thank the person, say goodbye, and call close_call once with outcome not_reached and reason callback."},{"source_ids":["brief-a:32","brief-a:41","brief-a:46"],"scenario":"A verified customer mentions job loss, then independently proposes a valid amount/date and accepts support. transfer_to_agent(queue=support) returns data.ok=true, but negotiation has no deterministic success route to close_stage; a semantic mismatch leaves it in negotiation.","expected_output":"Record the valid promise if confirmed and create_promise succeeds; transfer to support, then close once as transferred/support."},{"source_ids":["brief-a:37","brief-a:46"],"scenario":"A verified customer confirms valid terms. First create_promise returns data.ok=false; the next turn's always transition leaves the model in negotiation without an attempt counter or deterministic retry route. It can abandon the retry or repeat dialogue instead.","expected_output":"Retry create_promise once. If the second actual result is also unsuccessful, say it could not be recorded and close no_promise/service_error."},{"source_ids":["brief-a:14","brief-a:46"],"scenario":"The third wrong security answer returns wrong_answers_left=0. Extraction labels the turn other or uncertain, so the matches_intent terminal route does not match and the always route repeats identity questions.","expected_output":"Stop verification, say to use the mobile app or a branch, and close not_verified/failed without disclosing the debt."}]}
